subject: SIG / SOC 2 evidence sprint — control ownership runbook & kickoff
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG / SOC 2 evidence sprint — runbook & kickoff

Team —

Silverline procurement just triggered a full SIG questionnaire (they flagged SOC 2 + ISO Annex A mapping) and want control-level evidence within 7 business days. Their intake is authenticated procure@silverline.com; contact is Alice Gomez in procurement.

I need a short, executable runbook we can give them that: (1) maps Redwood controls to SIG sections, (2) calls out asset owners and evidence artifacts, and (3) lists exact log snippets / time ranges we can deliver. Goal: get comfortable commit for required artifacts by EOD tomorrow so we can schedule the evidence upload sprint early next week.

Initial asks:
- Karthik: lead control mapping (SOC 2/ISO alignment). Pull the latest control map and identify any controls without a clear artifact.
- Marissa: lead artifact collection (evidence owner liaison & packaging). We need file-level names and custodians for each artifact.
- Ben: SIEM / key rotation logs & sampling — produce 30-day examples for the controls that require operational proof.

I'll draft the runbook and a packaging checklist; attaching a blank control_ownership_runbook.docx for you to annotate. We'll consolidate and send a single ZIP to Alice.

Thanks — KP

--
Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions Security
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@silverline.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, procure@silverline.com
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 10:05:24 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG / SOC 2 evidence sprint — questionnaire attached

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick reply. Attaching our SIG questionnaire (master workbook) — we try to be prescriptive about required artifact types: policy excerpts, configuration screenshots with timestamps, SIEM query output with hash or truncation markers, and a minimal set of host/instance identifiers.

Two quick clarifications before you begin:
1) We prefer artifacts with redacted PII but full metadata (timestamps, hostnames, UUIDs).
2) For key lifecycle proofs (KMS/HSM), a 30-day rotation history and a signed key provenance statement is sufficient.

My procurement inbox will collect the ZIP. If you can give us a target upload window by Friday 5pm PT, that would be ideal.

Alice Gomez
Senior Procurement Manager, Silverline Financial
procure@silverline.com
(415) 555-0199

Attachment: SIG_Questionnaire_v3.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 11:33:50 -0700
Subject: RE: SIG / SOC 2 evidence sprint — control mapping kickoff

Kimberly / team —

I've started an initial mapping against the SIG workbook. High-level notes:
- SOC 2 CC1-CC7 map cleanly to our existing SOC 2 scope; ISO A.5-A.18 mapping is straightforward for most administrative controls.
- Three areas flagged as potential gaps where we need explicit artifacts:
  * Key rotation provenance (ISO A.10.1): we have rotation records but need a signed statement linked to the KMS audit trail.
  * Third-party data processing exceptions (ISO A.15): need updated vendor attestation or contract appendix for our telemetry processor.
  * System change control (ISO A.12.1): change ticket snapshots are there, but some older tickets lack the post-deploy verification artifact.

I'll populate control_ownership_runbook.docx with owners for each control and mark the required artifact type per Alice's guidance. Expect first pass by 4pm PT.

Karthik
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 14:07:12 -0700
Subject: RE: SIG / SOC 2 evidence sprint — packaging plan

Adding packaging notes and a suggested upload structure:

Suggested ZIP layout:
- /SIG-Submission/metadata.json (index with control -> filename mapping)
- /SIG-Submission/policies/ (policy PDFs with control ref)
- /SIG-Submission/logs/ (SIEM extracts; CSVs/TSV; truncated with hash)
- /SIG-Submission/keys/ (rotation history export + provenance statements)
- /SIG-Submission/thirdparty/ (vendor attestations, signed addenda)

I've started pulling the following artifacts locally:
- Policy: "Access Control Policy v2.1.pdf" (owner: Legal / Marissa)
- Change tickets export: "chg_tickets_apr-jul.csv" (owner: EngOps)

Two asks for Ben:
1) For SIEM attachments, can you include the exact query used as the first line of the file and a 30-day window ending Aug 15?
2) For key rotation: provide the key rotation audit export and one example KMS log that shows rotation event metadata.

I'll annotate the runbook with file names and owners; please comment in the docx.

-Marissa
Senior Assurance Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 16:22:44 -0700
Subject: RE: SIG / SOC 2 evidence sprint — SIEM & KMS samples

Marissa / team —

Attached: siem_kv_rotation_snippet.zip contains:
- siem_query_userauth_30d.csv (first line = "SELECT timestamp, username, src_ip, event_id FROM user_auth WHERE timestamp >= '2028-07-17' AND timestamp <= '2028-08-15' LIMIT 1000")
- kms_rotation_30d.log (sample rotation events with rotation_id, key_id, timestamp, actor) — redacted PII, hostnames left intact
- readme.txt (controls covered: SIG.Control.1.5, SIG.Control.3.2, SOC2.CC6)

Notes:
- The KMS export has been signed by CloudOps as an authenticity statement (see signed_stamp in readme). I'll add a brief provenance paragraph to the runbook linking to the audit ticket.
- I found 2 change tickets (May 2027) missing explicit post-deploy verification; flagged those in the docx so Marissa can ask EngOps for the missing evidence.

Ben
Security Operations, Redwood Inference
